target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 15, “Fine scale of the growth behaviour.” This is the open problem asking for an exponent β determined by Banach-space geometry in the decay estimate for ‖T(t)A^{-1}‖ under polynomial resolvent growth. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct ambient setting and almost all of the official hypotheses: a bounded C0-semigroup (T(t))t≥0 on a complex Banach space X, generator A, the spectral assumption σ(A)∩iℝ=∅, polynomial resolvent growth ‖(is−A)−1‖=O(|s|^α) as |s|→∞, and the idea that the optimal logarithmic loss should depend on geometric properties of X such as Fourier type, type, or cotype. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
missing_details: The paper’s problem asks for β in the interval [0,1]; your draft leaves the target set for β unspecified. The adjoining comments explain why this interval is the intended scope. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

The concluding estimate is garbled in your draft. The paper’s statement is ‖T(t)A^{-1}‖ = O((log t)^(β/α) / t^(1/α)) as t→∞. In particular, the operator is A^{-1}, not A, and the logarithmic factor is in the numerator. ([nnov.hse.ru](https://nnov.hse.ru/data/2022/02/18/1747622281/Open_problems_in_OPSO_theory_part_1.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should specify that all norms are operator norms on L(X). This is implicit in the paper’s notation. ([nnov.hse.ru](https://nnov.hse.ru/data/2022/02/18/1747622281/Open_problems_in_OPSO_theory_part_1.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Because 0∈iℝ, the assumption σ(A)∩iℝ=∅ implies 0∉σ(A), so A^{-1} exists; this is hidden in the paper’s shorthand and should be made explicit in a self-contained rewrite. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

The paper asks for β to depend on geometric properties of the Banach space X itself (for example Fourier type, type, or cotype), not merely for some ad hoc exponent attached to a single semigroup. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

The nearby comments supply important scope restrictions: β=1 is always admissible in general Banach spaces, β<0 is impossible in general, and β=0 is available on Hilbert spaces. These facts are not hypotheses, but they are part of the paper-faithful formulation of what remains open. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

For full self-containment, it is helpful to say explicitly that “bounded C0-semigroup” means sup_{t≥0}‖T(t)‖<∞ and that A is the generator of this semigroup. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
refined_question: Let (T(t))_{t≥0} be a bounded C0-semigroup on a complex Banach space X, with generator A. Assume that σ(A)∩iℝ=∅, so in particular A^{-1} exists, and that there is an α>0 such that ‖(is−A)^{-1}‖=O(|s|^α) as |s|→∞. Determine an exponent β=β(X)∈[0,1], in terms of geometric properties of X (for instance its Fourier type, type, or cotype), such that the operator-norm decay estimate ‖T(t)A^{-1}‖=O((log t)^(β/α)/t^(1/α)) holds as t→∞.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper almost verbatim: it matches Section 3, Problem 15 rather than a broader neighboring problem. The main corrections needed are to restore the exact decay formula, to replace A by A^{-1} in that formula, and to include the paper’s intended range β∈[0,1]. The comments immediately following Problem 15 also define the paper’s exact scope by recording the known endpoint facts β=1 in general Banach spaces and β=0 on Hilbert spaces, showing that the real open issue is how geometry of X improves the logarithmic loss. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
